comparison_baseline.identity_scope: Caller-declared source; actual binary SHA256 is recorded separately.

underlying_plan_selector.scope: Selects the existing six-default-pairs-per-CPU schedule only. It does not establish EE binary/source identity for a non-EE comparison.

tool_provenance.scope: Nine original files byte-copied without changes; same oracle and measurements plus original launcher. metrics.py contains exact original standard_metrics function only. Historical source HEAD is not a retained runtime recommendation. Scoped .gitattributes -text preserves original vendor bytes across platforms.

files.extraction: standard_metrics function copied verbatim, imports limited to its dependencies

notes: EE-only 12-pair initial screen. Omits retained-R default, spill and wide protection; never the historical 24-pair release gate.
Original deterministic generator, sampled independent TopK oracle, all restarted IDs and sampled vectors are unchanged.
Full responses compared by SHA256 across each pair; per-request timings, phase counters, memory and IO remain in raw reports.
First-lifecycle wall is the sum of original measured request/startup/shutdown intervals. CPU ends before shutdown, as in the historical metric.
CPU counters include engine activity during client checks. Driver/oracle remain outside DB cgroup, sharing the same host.
Warm OS cache; no cache dropping or discarded warmup samples. Failure stops this screen and preserves completed/partial data.
No numeric official-score forecast. Source-to-ELF build provenance must be established separately.

1.raw_plan_scope: Unmodified historical helper uses an ee selector/family label for this six-pair schedule; source and binary identity are the explicit identities records, not that plan label.

thread_policy_observations.scope: Observed decisions and task counters. Nonmain CPU is not exclusively query worker CPU.

limitations: Diagnostic only: requested one/two-CPU and memory/swap limits are explicit, not a verified official resource envelope. Ancestor constraints are retained.
DB quota and selected affinity are explicit; affinity is checked after every ready. Driver affinity is unchanged; driver/oracle stay outside DB cgroup but share host resources.
Comparison kind and both binary/source/environment identities are explicit. A version contrast includes compiler/layout effects; neither comparison proves the official binary identity.

Highest-primary screen: six EE default pairs or four retained default plus two protection pairs at this CPU count. One seed, no automatic adoption or score conversion. EE is a verified original-source rebuild, not the recovered official executable.
Cgroup totals include DB restart verification, filesystem page cache and static launcher; request timers exclude independent oracle work.
Ready timing includes membership/executable/affinity evidence reads. Projection phase snapshots are outside individual request timers.
Phase task snapshots retain TID/starttime/CPU ticks/affinity. Nonmain CPU includes parser work; it is not exclusively query-worker CPU.
IO counters use the shared host filesystem; bounded post-exit stability is not dedicated-device writeback proof.
Iteration keeps its existing first/second/last TopK oracle, all restart IDs and sampled vectors; write-query and projection retain their stronger full oracles.
Base iteration errors may not expose partial phase timers; adapter preserves transport count, stderr, cgroup evidence and preceding completed side.

2.raw_plan_scope: Unmodified historical helper uses an ee selector/family label for this six-pair schedule; source and binary identity are the explicit identities records, not that plan label.

thread_policy_observations.scope: Observed decisions and task counters. Nonmain CPU is not exclusively query worker CPU.

limitations: Diagnostic only: requested one/two-CPU and memory/swap limits are explicit, not a verified official resource envelope. Ancestor constraints are retained.
DB quota and selected affinity are explicit; affinity is checked after every ready. Driver affinity is unchanged; driver/oracle stay outside DB cgroup but share host resources.
Comparison kind and both binary/source/environment identities are explicit. A version contrast includes compiler/layout effects; neither comparison proves the official binary identity.

Highest-primary screen: six EE default pairs or four retained default plus two protection pairs at this CPU count. One seed, no automatic adoption or score conversion. EE is a verified original-source rebuild, not the recovered official executable.
Cgroup totals include DB restart verification, filesystem page cache and static launcher; request timers exclude independent oracle work.
Ready timing includes membership/executable/affinity evidence reads. Projection phase snapshots are outside individual request timers.
Phase task snapshots retain TID/starttime/CPU ticks/affinity. Nonmain CPU includes parser work; it is not exclusively query-worker CPU.
IO counters use the shared host filesystem; bounded post-exit stability is not dedicated-device writeback proof.
Iteration keeps its existing first/second/last TopK oracle, all restart IDs and sampled vectors; write-query and projection retain their stronger full oracles.
Base iteration errors may not expose partial phase timers; adapter preserves transport count, stderr, cgroup evidence and preceding completed side.
